name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Counter-BCI Rifle ACBR-2 'Migraine'
description:
The ACBR-2 Migraine is a designated marksman rifle that fires a specialized round containing a focused EMP micro-charge alongside a conventional 6.5mm penetrator. On impact, the projectile delivers ballistic damage while simultaneously emitting a localized electromagnetic pulse designed to disrupt BCI implants within a 2-meter radius of the impact point. Against BCI-augmented targets, the Migraine inflicts both physical trauma and neural interface disruption — a combination that is incapacitating even if the ballistic wound is survivable.

The rifle's BCI-ironic design — using smart-link technology to deliver anti-BCI weapons — is built on Arcturus' standard DMR platform with a modified barrel to accommodate the larger EMP-carrying projectile. The smart-scope provides targeting that identifies BCI-augmented targets by detecting the electromagnetic emissions of active neural interfaces, effectively locating targets by their cybernetic enhancements.

Arcturus developed the Migraine for counter-augmentation operations — engaging targets whose BCI-linked weapons, neural armor, or cybernetic enhancements provide tactical advantages that conventional weapons cannot neutralize. At Φ12,000, plus Φ50 per specialized round, the weapon is expensive to field. Its customers view the cost as worthwhile insurance against BCI-dependent opponents whose entire combat capability collapses when their neural interface goes dark.
specifications:
caliber: 6.5mm EMP-carrier
effective_range: 600m
rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic
magazine_capacity: 15 rounds
weight: 4.8 kg
tactical_use: The Migraine neutralizes BCI-dependent combatants by disrupting the technology they rely on. A single hit disables BCI-linked weapons, neural targeting aids, communication systems, and cybernetic enhancements within the EMP blast radius. Against heavily augmented opponents, this disruption is often more tactically significant than the ballistic wound itself. The BCI emission detection scope allows the marksman to identify and prioritize the most heavily augmented targets in a group.
cultural_context: The Migraine is a weapon designed to punish augmentation. In a world where BCI integration provides overwhelming tactical advantages, the ACBR-2 represents the counter — a reminder that dependence on technology creates vulnerability. Anti-augmentation groups celebrate the Migraine as proof that the augmented are not invulnerable. Augmented communities view it as a targeted weapon of prejudice, designed specifically to harm people for their cybernetic choices.
story_hooks: A Migraine round struck an augmented civilian bystander, and the EMP disrupted their life-sustaining medical cyberware. The target survived; the bystander did not. The weapon's indiscriminate EMP radius is now a legal liability issue.
An augmented rights group has obtained a Migraine and is publicly destroying it in a media event. Arcturus is calculating whether the publicity is more damaging than the loss of a single weapon.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, angular designated marksman rifle with a distinctly predatory stance. The receiver is dominated by a prominent thermal management shroud running the length of the barrel, with subtle electromagnetic shielding visible as faint geometric ribbing. The overall silhouette reads as purposeful and clinical — all business, no ornamentation.
physical_description.dimensions: Total length: 112 cm | Barrel length: 56 cm | Receiver width: 8.2 cm | Height with scope: 18 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Substantial and well-balanced — 4.8 kg distributes evenly across the platform, making the rifle feel planted rather than heavy. The forward weight bias from the modified barrel and EMP chamber gives it a confident, stable feel in the shoulder.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade carbon composite receiver with reinforced steel barrel jacket. The thermal shroud is anodized aluminum. Internal components use electromagnetic-shielded steel.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal with brushed steel accents on the barrel and action. The thermal management shroud features a subtle gunmetal gradient that catches light, hinting at the electromagnetic systems within.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: matte charcoal gray | Accents: brushed gunmetal steel, faint copper-bronze heat-dissipation scoring on the shroud | Scope: blackened titanium with faint amber illumination from BCI-detection indicators
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip with embedded conductive trace patterns — designed to interface with operator's glove-mounted neural link for targeting handoff. Slightly tacky, anti-slip finish with subtle grid pattern.
distinctive_features: Modified barrel chamber visibly larger than standard 6.5mm specification, housing the EMP-carrier projectile
Thermal management shroud with geometric ribbing that doubles as electromagnetic shielding
Integrated BCI emission detection scope with amber LED indicators that pulse when active targets are detected
Secondary charging port (recessed into left side of receiver) for pre-charging EMP rounds — barely visible but tactilely distinct
Stabilization rail running dorsally along the receiver with weapon-mounted neural link interface point
Subtle Arcturus Defense Solutions logo etched in matte finish on the charging handle
Heat scoring and faint copper oxidation patterns on the shroud from repeated EMP discharge
Magazine well designed for the slightly longer EMP-carrier round — visibly deeper than standard DMR magazines
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Arcturus Defense Solutions logo — a stylized angular 'A' — etched in matte finish on the charging handle. Serial number and regulatory compliance stamps appear on a discrete titanium plate welded to the left side of the receiver, positioned so they're only visible during field maintenance.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained operational condition with visible use. Light scorching around the muzzle brake from EMP discharge. Grip shows contact wear from gloved operation. The shroud exhibits faint heat-stress patina and oxidation scoring that suggests frequent thermal cycling — evidence of regular deployment.
